extracted.intended_audience: newspaper readers, journalists, and civic/municipal officials
extracted.subtask_description: Short news reports and briefs covering municipal meetings, ordinances, civic conventions, and community organizations; includes reporting of proposed laws, committee recommendations, and public reactions. Primarily example items for news-homepage style municipal coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chicken coop distance regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: "a chicken coop could not be kept within seventy-five feet of a factory."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation framed to protect sanitation-sensitive "factories" such as milk-bottling works; enforcement discussion includes intent not to discriminate and comparisons with other distance rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saloons distance regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Saloons are required to be 200 feet removed from the nearest church or school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a comparative justification for the poultry-distance rule; invoked in debates about whether spacing rules are discriminatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slaughterhouse regulation enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assertion that 150,000 chickens were slaughtered in New York City every year in violation of the law regulating slaughter houses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raises enforcement and public-health concerns; some chicken owners argue private slaughtering is "more sanitary" than licensed slaughterhouses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justices of the Peace bill — election and jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Justices of the Peace shall be elected at large in St. Louis and each shall have jurisdiction throughout the city.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of a reform package modeled on municipal courts to reduce political patronage and centralized jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justices of the Peace bill — qualifications and number
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill provides for a reduction in the number of Justices from 11 to 7; each Justice must be a licensed attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed at ending practice of ward politicians electing themselves; qualification requirement intended to professionalize the bench.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justices of the Peace bill — compensation and offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Justice placed on a salary of $3000 a year; one Constable provided at $2500 a year; deputy clerks and Constables to be paid $1800 a year each; Constable allowed 2½ per cent of all amounts collected by him on execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies remuneration and fee structure to replace patronage-based pay and to centralize administrative functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justices of the Peace bill — clerks and facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: One clerk is provided for, to be elected by the Justices; the Board of Aldermen shall provide suitable rooms and offices, centrally located.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses staffing and physical-location requirements without requiring all courts in one building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevated railway ordinance — approval, tender, and construction timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Work shall be started within six months after the plans have been approved by the Departments of Public Works and of City Transit; if the Philadelphia Rapid Transit Company does not indicate acceptance within 90 days after passage, the Mayor shall request tenders; successful tenderer given six months to present complete plans and six months after approval to start construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets explicit administrative deadlines and a fallback tendering process to ensure timely project initiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevated railway ordinance — franchise financial and fare terms
rubrics_metrics.description: In consideration of the franchise the company is to pay to the city 10 per cent of its net profits in cash before any dividends are paid; the rate of fare is not to exceed 5 cents for a continuous ride.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies city share of profits and a maximum fare cap as conditions of the franchise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevated railway ordinance — technical specifications and route
rubrics_metrics.description: The road throughout is to have an overhead clearance of 14 feet above street grades; to be operated by electricity or any power other than steam; route and stations explicitly enumerated (Front & Arch to Rhawn, with specified intermediate stations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets engineering and route-specific standards that the operator must meet; route chosen may affect broader transit planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transit planning principle — system-wide integration and transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that an ordinance which does not embrace transit facilities "on a broad basis" and which provides no provision for transfers will defeat plans to connect city sections with high-speed lines for a single fare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy criterion: transit projects should be planned as an integrated system with transfer provisions to avoid multiple fares and fragmentation of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of blood-pressure monitoring to detect deception
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim by Dr. Louisa Burns that no one can tell a lie under close physiological observation without an increase in the pressure of the blood; pulse action is an indicator beyond voluntary control and can reveal concealed facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes a technique of observing pulse/blood pressure during conversational questioning, preferring patient to lie on a table and not be distracted; practitioner cautions about using such testimony in court despite confidence in method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Railway safety — juvenile diversion via incentives and amenities
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedy for boys who play with rolling stock: award 'Safety' buttons to those who swear off dangerous pastimes, and, if needed, install swimming pools near round-houses under railroad supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical safety strategy combining recognition/incentives and provision of supervised recreational outlets to reduce hazardous behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Council resolution — elimination of alcoholic stimulants among employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolution: 'It is recognized that the use of alcoholic stimulants is productive of most industrial accidents... Therefore... the members pledge themselves to the elimination of the use of alcoholic stimulants among the employees of their plants and factories.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational policy recommending abstention from alcohol in the workplace as an accident-prevention measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety education across schooling levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that the inculcation of accident prevention should start in the kindergarten and continue through high school and college.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates long-term public education to instill safety attitudes and reduce accidents over the life course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer responsibility for workplace safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Assertion that 75 per cent of factory accidents are due to the disinterested and indifferent attitude of the employer toward his employee; 'Safety first is a hard practicality of business extension.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames safety as both moral and economic duty of employers; suggests employer engagement is central to accident reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Railway commissions — ventilation and coach lighting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: "More deaths are caused by improper ventilation of train coaches and waiting rooms than by train accidents." Committee recommends vigorous campaign against dingy oil lamps on branch lines and improved ventilation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-health and comfort standards: improve ventilation especially in sleeping cars and eliminate inadequate lighting on branch lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Railway commissions — drinking-water sanitation practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to abolish the stationary water cooler and prescribe a cooler with a portable container; require uniform methods of cleansing such containers, sanitary handling of ice, and sanitary drinking cups provided free to the public; placing ice in the receptacle is deprecated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanitary-prescription for potable water and ice handling at stations and on trains to reduce germ transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Railway commissions — minimum Sunday service
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee belief that at least one train should operate in each direction as a minimum Sunday service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service-level standard to ensure basic mobility on Sundays where lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Railway commissions — freight-claims handling and interest on claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to eliminate practice of paying freight bills carrying manifest over charges; to minimize delays in handling and settling claims require railroads to pay interest on the true claim amount from the date the amount went into their hands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative-financial reforms aimed at faster, fairer claims settlement and discouraging overcharges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Railway commissions — equipment standards and regulatory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that the Interstate Commerce Commission be given full power to prescribe the character of equipment to be used in interstate commerce; substitution of steel for wooden cars recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical-safety standard advocating stronger federal authority to mandate safer rolling stock (e.g., steel cars) for interstate trains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old-clothes dealers' equal enforcement complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Pedlers complain the anti-noise police mandate muzzled their street cries but has not been applied to the permanent exchange at Bayard and Elizabeth streets; they ask for equal application or mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion of equal and even-handed enforcement of municipal noise regulations across itinerant and established markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quaker (Friends') meeting conduct — unhurried, quiet fellowship
rubrics_metrics.description: Meeting characterized by soft stillness, unhurried reading of messages, emphasis on "One for another," and a preference for slow courtesy and quiet communion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptive guideline for conduct of worship/meeting: keep meetings slow, quiet, focused on fellowship, messages, and mutual love.
